site.name: Trigonometry Playground
site.description: Interactive trigonometry labs for students: right triangles, the unit circle, graphs, the laws of sines and cosines, angle-sum formulas and identities. Nothing to install.

home.heroTitle: Spinning angles, waves that draw themselves
home.heroText: Trigonometry is a dance between a circle and a spinning right triangle. Drag, spin and match, and see for yourself where the formulas come from.
home.heroArtLabel: A point goes round a circle. Its height draws a wave next to it: the graph of the sine function.
home.chooseText: They are in order: each one builds on the one before. The stars show how hard each one is.

ratios.title: The right triangle
ratios.blurb: Sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of sides. And how tall is that tower?
ratios.lead: Drag the top corner of the triangle. Watch the three ratios: they change when you change the angle, but not when you make the triangle bigger.

unit-circle.title: The unit circle
unit-circle.blurb: A point spins round a circle of radius 1. Its height is the sine, and its sideways distance is the cosine.
unit-circle.lead: Drag the point round the circle or press “Spin”. The point’s height (red) is drawn next to it: that is the graph of sin x.

waves.title: The wave maker
waves.blurb: y = A·sin(bx + φ) + k. Each letter does exactly one thing to the graph. Can you match the wave?
waves.lead: Move the sliders and watch what each letter does: A stretches up and down, b squeezes sideways, φ slides left or right, and k lifts the graph up or down.

triangles.title: Any triangle
triangles.blurb: The law of sines, the law of cosines, and five area formulas that always give the same number.
triangles.lead: Drag corners A, B and C anywhere. The formulas on the right update as you go, and they agree every time.

angle-sum.title: sin(A + B), step by step
angle-sum.blurb: Why isn’t sin(A+B) just sin A + sin B? Build the proof from a picture.
angle-sum.lead: This is the proof from the lesson packet, drawn one step at a time. Change angles A and B: the picture redraws itself and the equation stays true.

identities.title: Identity or impostor?
identities.blurb: Some formulas are true for every angle; others only look true. The graphs give them away.
identities.lead: Read the formula and guess: is it true for every x, or is it an impostor? Then both sides are drawn. A real identity draws the same curve twice.

footer.credit: The lessons follow Brent Hughes’s trigonometry packet.

quiz.scorePerfect: Perfect! You’re ready for the bonus questions.
quiz.scoreGood: Well done! Read the explanations again for the ones you missed.
quiz.scoreLow: No problem: play in the lab for a bit, then try the quiz again.
quiz.bonusTitle: Bonus questions for a trained mind
quiz.bonusIntro: These have no options. Think, talk it over with someone, then look at the answer.
quiz.intro: {total} questions. Pick an answer and press “Check”.

ratios.sceneLabel: A right triangle with angle θ of {a} degrees.
ratios.dragCorner: Top corner of the triangle. Move it with the arrow keys.
ratios.towerSceneLabel: A child looks up at the top of a tower. The distance to the tower and the angle of the gaze are known.
ratios.sizeNote: You changed the size, but sin, cos and tan stayed the same! The ratios depend only on the angle. That’s why they fit in a table.
ratios.mnemonic: Remember SOH-CAH-TOA: Sin = Opposite / Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent / Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite / Adjacent.
ratios.pythText: Divide Pythagoras’ theorem by hypotenuse² and you get the most important identity in trigonometry: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
ratios.towerText: You stand {d} m from a tower and see its top at an angle of {a}°. How tall is the tower?
ratios.towerTable: From the table: tan {a}° ≈ {t}. Hint: tan θ = opposite / adjacent = height / distance.
ratios.towerExplain: Height = {d} · tan {a}° ≈ {h} m. This is how surveyors measured mountains and buildings without climbing them.
ratios.towerWrong: Not yet. Multiply the distance by the tangent of the angle.

unitCircle.sceneLabel: The unit circle. The angle θ is {a} degrees; sin θ = {s}, cos θ = {c}.
unitCircle.valuesNote: The radius is 1, so the hypotenuse drops out of the ratios: sin θ is simply the height and cos θ simply the sideways distance.
unitCircle.foundText: Yes! θ = {a}°. Look at the signs: which quadrant are you in?
unitCircle.challengeHint: Move the point until you reach an angle that fits. Use the signs in each quadrant.
unitCircle.challengeIntro: I give you a value and a sign. You find the angle on the circle.

waves.sceneLabel: The graph of the function, with the basic graph dotted behind it.
waves.noAmplitude: tan has none (it climbs to infinity)
waves.matchedText: Well done! Your wave sits exactly on the orange one.
waves.gameHint: Move the sliders until your line lies exactly on the orange band.
waves.gameIntro: An orange wave appears. Find A, b, φ and k to cover it exactly.

triangles.sceneLabel: A triangle with angles A = {A}°, B = {B}° and C = {C}°.
triangles.corner: Corner {c}. Move it with the arrow keys.
triangles.sinesText: Each side divided by the sine of the opposite angle gives the same number: the diameter of the circle through all three corners.
triangles.cosinesRight: The angle is 90° and cos 90° = 0, so the last term vanishes and Pythagoras’ theorem is left!
triangles.cosinesObtuse: The angle is over 90°, so its cosine is negative: the opposite side comes out longer than Pythagoras would give.
triangles.cosinesText: It is Pythagoras’ theorem with a correction for angles that aren’t right angles. Try making the angle 90°.
triangles.areaText: They look very different, but they all give the same number. They all start from ½ · base · height.
triangles.tip: Try making a 3-4-5 triangle: one side 3 squares, one 4 squares, and a right angle between them.

angleSum.sceneLabel: Proof of the sin(A+B) formula, step {step}. A = {a}°, B = {b}°.
angleSum.step1: Radius OP has length 1 and angle A + B. P’s height is sin(A+B) and its sideways distance is cos(A+B). We want to write them using only sin A, cos A, sin B and cos B.
angleSum.step2: Draw the line at angle A, and drop a perpendicular from P onto it, at Q. Triangle OQP has a right angle at Q, angle B at O, and hypotenuse 1. So OQ = cos B and QP = sin B.
angleSum.step3: The triangle under OQ has hypotenuse cos B and angle A. Q’s height is cos B · sin A (purple), and its sideways distance is cos B · cos A (light blue).
angleSum.step4: The small triangle next to P has hypotenuse QP = sin B, and its top angle is A again (QP is perpendicular to OQ, and the vertical is perpendicular to the horizontal). The climb from Q up to P is sin B · cos A (orange). The step back to the left is sin B · sin A (green).
angleSum.step5: P’s height is Q’s height plus the climb up to P. P’s distance is Q’s distance minus the green piece. Those are the angle-sum formulas!
angleSum.done: Swap B for −B and you get sin(A−B) and cos(A−B) for free. Put B = A and you get sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A.

identities.sceneLabel: Graphs of both sides of the formula, drawn on top of each other.
identities.guessFirst: Guess first, then the graphs appear.
identities.question: Is it true for every x?
identities.isReal: It’s an identity: the two curves lie on top of each other for every x.
identities.isFake: It’s an impostor: the curves come apart.
identities.counter: At x = {x}°: left = {f}, right = {g}. One counterexample is enough.
identities.exploreText: Formulas marked ✗ are impostors. Move x and see where the curves come apart.
identities.legend: The red band is the left side; the dotted blue line is the right side.
